newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MARLINS' NEAR PERFECT BROWN SETTLES FOR NO-HITTER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MARLINS' NEAR PERFECT BROWN SETTLES FOR NO-HITTER.

text.p: Florida Marlins pitcher Kevin Brown flirted with perfection before settling for a no-hitter against the San Francisco Giants on Tuesday.
Brown became the first player in the majors to throw a no-hitter this year in a 9-0 rout of San Francisco.
He came within four outs of a perfect game before hitting Marvin Benard with a 1-2 pitch with two out in the eighth inning, then mowed down the last four batters.
Brown walked none and struck out seven in recording the second no-hitter in Florida franchise history.
"I've seen some great pitching in my day -- this ranks right up there with the all-time bests," said Marlins manager Jim Leyland. "This was a dominant no-hitter, it was not a fluke."
In a 99-pitch masterpiece that featured 68 strikes and only five pitches clocked below 90 miles per hour (145 kph), Brown allowed the Giants only three balls out of the infield.
The game started as a classic pitchers' duel with San Francisco's William VanLandingham (3-4) also pitching a no-hitter for the first six innings, despite allowing a run.

In the seventh, VanLandingham came undone. After walking Bobby Bonilla, catcher Charles Johnson smoked a pitch over the left-field fence, giving the Marlins a 3-0 lead. Before Florida was finished they had scored seven runs in the inning.
"This was a huge thrill," said Johnson of breaking up one no-hitter and catching another. "It's a part of history and I'll cherish it forever."

At Colorado, Chipper Jones delivered a two-run single off Kevin Ritz to key a four-run fifth inning and Denny Neagle allowed three runs over seven innings to lead the Atlanta Braves to an 8-3 victory over the Rockies.
Javier Lopez, whose RBI double in the fifth extended Atlanta's lead to 6-1, had three hits, including two doubles.
Jones, who drove in four runs and scored twice, launched a 460-foot solo homer into the upper deck in right in the ninth.
Neagle (9-1) allowed five hits and walked five with three strikeouts to post the win. Ritz (5-5) took the loss.
In Chicago, the Mets got home runs from their entire infield as New York pounded the Cubs 10-6.

First baseman John Olerud and shortstop Manny Alexander homered off Cubs starter Kevin Foster (7-4) as the Mets built an 8-1 lead. Third baseman Edgardo Alfonzo and second baseman Carlos Baerga added solo homers in the eighth and ninth innings, respectively, for New York.

Dave Mlicki (2-5) held the Cubs to a run through the first four innings before tiring in the fifth. He gave up five runs and 11 hits. Four Met relievers combined to allow just one hit -- a homer by Sammy Sosa -- over the final four frames.
In Cincinnati, pitcher Rich Loiselle's error allowed the tying and go-ahead runs to score in a four-run eighth inning that rallied the Reds to an 8-5 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates.
Pittsburgh jumped out to a 5-0 lead with a five-run second against Cincinnati starter Dave Burba. But the Reds chipped away to get within 5-4 after seven innings.

In the eighth with the bases loaded, Barry Larkin hit a grounder to Mark Johnson, but Loiselle could not handle the first baseman's throw, which went into the dugout and allowed two runs to score, giving the Reds the lead for good.
In Montreal, Mike Lansing's two-run single snapped a tie as the Expos used a four-run, eighth-inning rally against closer Ricky Bottalico (1-2) to claim an 8-5 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies.

Philadelphia took a 5-4 lead into the eighth. But Joe Orsulak tripled and survived a run down when a throw hit him in the back. He scored the tying run when Andy Stankiewicz, hitting for Expos reliever Dave Veres (2-1), blooped a double to centre field.
Lansing's RBI single scored Ryan McGuire and Stankiewicz to seal the Expos' fifth consecutive victory.
In Los Angeles, Craig Biggio snapped an eighth-inning tie with a three-run double and Jeff Bagwell had three hits and two RBI as the Houston Astros beat the Dodgers 6-3.

Dodgers reliever Antonio Osuna (1-2) was brought in to keep the game tied at 2-2. But he loaded the bases and with two out, Biggio lined the ball off the wall in left-centre, clearing the bases for a 5-2 lead. Thomas Howard capped the outburst with an RBI single.
"Biggio's hit was huge, all year long we've lacked that knockout punch," Astros manager Larry Dierker said.
Mike Magnante (2-0) picked up the victory.
In San Diego, Chris Gomez's one-out single in the bottom of the 12th inning scored Wally Joyner with the winning run as the Padres edged the St Louis Cardinals 6-5.
Delino DeShields' two-run homer capped a four-run, ninth-inning rally against Padres closer Trevor Hoffman as the Cardinals turned a two-run deficit into a 5-3 lead.

But the Padres rallied in the bottom of the frame on a two-out, two-run double by Tony Gwynn off St Louis closer Dennis Eckersley. Gwynn, who had three doubles, extended his hitting streak to 20 games.
